newsitem.title: MEXICO: Raul Salinas laundered money, Mexico says.
newsitem.headline: Raul Salinas laundered money, Mexico says.

text.p: Mexican authorities said on Wednesday they had formally charged ex-president Carlos Salinas de Gortari's brother Raul for the first time with money laundering.

Raul Salinas has been imprisoned in Mexico City's maxiumum security Almoloya jail since February 1995 on charges of plotting the murder of a top politician and piling up an illicit fortune estimated at more than $100 million.
He has yet to be convincted of any crime.

The Attorney General's Office (PGR) said in a statement on Tuesday it had started a fresh court case against Salinas for allegedly laundering $13.7 million in ill-gotten gains. A PGR spokeswoman said on Wednesday this was the first formal charge filed against him for money laundering.

"Raul Salinas de Gortari carried out between January 1991 and April 1992 various financial operations, transfers and deposits of money in various bank accounts which were in his name, in the name of his dependants and of other non-existent people who it was later proved were false names," the statement said.
"The accused, knowing the money was the result of his own illegal enrichment, carried out the operations in order to disguise the origin of the money."

The statement did not say where the illicit cash came from but the period it mentioned began immediately after Salinas concluded a stint from December 1988 to November 1989 as head of planning at the government-owned food agency Conasupo.
The PGR spokeswoman was unable to say where the illicit money had come from but Reforma newspaper reported that the cash was from illegal operations with Conasupo.
Authorities are continuing a separate investigation into allegations that Salinas laundered or received drug money but no formal drug charges have been filed so far.
Salinas has strongly denied all the charges against him. He claims he is the victim of political persecuation by opponents of his brothers's 1988-94 administration.
Carlos Salinas, living in self-imposed exile in Dublin, has admitted that his brother "hurt the people" by piling up a huge fortune but says he is innocent of the murder charges.
